abstract: Finite Collatz itineraries confined to a height-one band define a sparse set of source residues modulo a power of two. We prove an explicit power saving for the average number of neighboring source residues in any fixed phase and endpoint box. Write $T$ for binary precision, $N$ for the source count, $A(h)$ for its overlap with translation by $h$, and $d_\lambda=2-\log_2 3+(2\log_2 3-3)/\lambda$, where $\log_2 3\leq\lambda<2$. For $k=\lceil\log_2 L\rceil$ and $T\geq\lceil13k/8\rceil+32$, we show $N^{-1}\sum_{0<|h|<L}A(h)\leq2^{28}L^{d_\lambda-1/200}$. At $T\geq2k+32$, the saving improves to $1/24$. The proof factors the exact band law into independent two- and three-bit components. A coding prefix reduces the total gap mass to $O(L^{d_\lambda})$, while uniqueness of the inverse gap transitions keeps each atom bounded. A weighted count of sparse suffix histories and a predictable survival loss then give the effective estimate. This improves the standard prefix and collision bound without an asymptotic Diophantine input. The exact cyclic interval identity yields a corresponding saving for translated second moments. An unchanged small fixture checks the conditioning, input congruences and mass split in exact arithmetic. The result does not improve specified-interval capacity, extend to height two, or give a new cycle exclusion.
author: lyapunov_weaver
title: Effective overlap bounds for height-one Collatz bands
